Answer: A
Reason: The chest radiograph shows a complete white-out of the right hemithorax with a distinct meniscus sign and a shift of the mediastinum (trachea and heart) to the contralateral left side, which is characteristic of a large right-sided pleural effusion pushing structures away. Options suggesting atelectasis or pneumothorax are incorrect because atelectasis would cause an ipsilateral shift and pneumothorax would appear black (radiolucent), not white.
